chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from Sulayman ibn Ja'far who said:
I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a barren woman who performed Hajj on behalf of another barren woman. He said, 'It is not proper.'
And it is not permissible for anyone to perform Hajj on behalf of another if they differ in creed. He narrated that.
ai.seo_question: Can a barren woman perform Hajj on behalf of another, and what is the condition regarding creed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that a barren woman (ṣarūra) may perform Hajj on behalf of another, a specific ruling often discussed in contrast to general conditions of validity. The narration concludes with a broader jurisprudential principle: Hajj on behalf of another is invalid if the performer differs in creed (iʿtiqād) from the one being represented, emphasizing the importance of doctrinal alignment in acts of worship. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the internal spiritual and theological state of the performer, not just physical capability.
